PullRequest.Title: sessions: badge the activity bar Changes entry on unseen changes and show its stats on hover
PullRequest.Body: ## What In the Agents window, the **Changes** entry of the Session Activity Bar now: - shows a **blue badge** (dot, `activityBarBadge` colors) over the icon's bottom-right corner — like the workbench activity bar — when the active chat has changes the user has not yet seen in the Changes tab; - shows the **same stats as the Changes pill** (` Files +ins -del`) in its hover and accessible label. ## How - **Activity service.** New `ISessionActivityBarActivityService` (`services/activity`) mirrors the workbench `IActivityService`: `showActivity(commandId, IActivity)` / `getActivity` / `onDidChangeActivity`, reusing the workbench `IActivity`/`IBadge` types. Every Session Activity Bar entry is now a `SessionActivityBarActionViewItem` that renders reported badges (count for `NumberBadge`, dot otherwise) and appends badge descriptions to its hover/aria label. - **Detecting new changes** (`contrib/changes/browser/changesActivity.ts`). Per chat, we remember the Changes pill stats last seen while the session's Changes tab was shown (side pane visible, or in an auxiliary window). The badge shows when the current stats differ and there are changed files. The first observation of a chat only seeds the baseline, and stats are ignored while not loaded yet (changeset loading, or only a summary is known — Copilot provider restores), so opening/restoring sessions does not badge. Seen state is persisted (application storage, LRU 200 chats). - **Hover.** The Changes entry uses a custom view item (via `IActionViewItemService`) that extends the core one and renders the pill stats in the pill's colors. - Accessibility help for the Session Activity Bar mentions the new label content. ## Notes for reviewers - Known limitation: edits that leave the exact file/line counts unchanged are not detected; reverting changes while not looking badges (stats differ from what was seen). - New fixture variant `sessionActivityBar/NewChanges` (Dark/Light/HC) — screenshot baselines need to be accepted from CI. ## Screenshots | Badge on unseen changes (live) | Hover shows the pill stats (live) | |---|---| | | | Badge across themes (fixture `sessionActivityBar/NewChanges`: Dark, Light, Dark HC, Light HC): ## Testing - Unit tests: activity service rendering/placement, seen-store persistence/eviction, contribution behavior (badge on unseen changes, cleared when the Changes tab is shown in the side pane or an auxiliary window, no badge for summary-only restores), loaded-stats helpers. `./scripts/test.sh` on the affected suites — 435 passing. - `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run hygiene`, ESLint, stylelint, `npm run valid-layers-check`, `npm run check-cyclic-dependencies` — clean. - Live in a dev build: a real agent turn with the Files tab active badges the entry; activating Changes clears it; reloading and visiting existing sessions (fresh seen state, side panel hidden) shows no false badges.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Both call paths and the collection-wide loop are explicit, and the provider's live file-edit observable proves repeated execution. Only the magnitude varies with turn size.
Findings.PerformanceResource: main-thread iterations over the active chat's complete changed-file array
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The diff adds two complete O(F) aggregations for each distinct file-edit snapshot (one through `pillStats`, one through `activeChanges`); over a turn that grows the list incrementally, the added work is O(U×F), approaching O(F²) when U tracks files added.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased main-thread latency and reduced responsiveness during large multi-file agent turns
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR the existing Changes pill/context consumers aggregated their own stats, but there was no activity contribution performing these two additional full-list reductions per active-chat update.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new contribution derives display stats and loaded activity stats independently from the same changed-file observable, causing duplicate complete aggregation whenever live file edits change.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 185 calls `readLoadedSessionInputPillStats` in `activeChanges`, while added lines 179-182 separately call `computeSessionInputPillStats` for the hover. Both reach `readChatChangesStats` and `readFileChangesStats`, whose loop sums every file.
Findings.Title: Reuse one aggregate for activity and hover stats
Findings.Impact: An agent editing tens or hundreds of files causes two extra complete scans on each changed edit snapshot, adding synchronous CPU on the UI thread exactly while the transcript and Changes UI are updating.
Findings.Evidence: `readLoadedSessionInputPillStats` calls `readLoadedChatChangesStats`, which calls `readChatChangesStats`; `computeSessionInputPillStats` also calls `readChatChangesStats`. Both end in `readFileChangesStats`'s loop over all changes. Agent-host `getLastTurnChanges` is driven by live chat-state file-edit snapshots and feeds the selected changeset, so this runs repeatedly during an active turn, not just once on open.
Findings.Recommendation: Create one shared derived result that contains loaded state plus aggregate stats, and derive both badge comparison and hover/cache fallback from it; do not invoke the full-file aggregation independently for `pillStats` and `activeChanges`.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The setting default and CSS-only visibility gate are explicit, and the new unconditional autoruns and storage path are directly traced. Exact milliseconds depend on turn size and update rate, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: main-thread CPU, temporary objects/serialized bytes, and application-storage updates
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows with active-chat change snapshots and changed-file count even when `sessions.showSessionActivityBar` is false; when Changes is visible it additionally grows with the persisted history (up to 200 chats) per snapshot.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: background CPU/GC pressure and storage churn for a disabled feature
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no changes-activity contribution, no seen-state storage, and no additional stats observers when the Session Activity Bar was disabled.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every desktop Agents window now observes active-session file-change snapshots and maintains seen state regardless of whether the Session Activity Bar is enabled or visible.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The new contribution's only early gate is the desktop-layout check at line 167; after it, the diff unconditionally installs `activeChanges`/badge autoruns, the persisted seen store, and the custom hover stats observer. The activity bar itself merely hides via `sessions.showSessionActivityBar`, whose stable-build default is false.
Findings.Title: Gate the activity observers on the activity-bar setting
Findings.Impact: On stable builds, where the activity bar defaults off, active agent turns that stream file-edit snapshots still perform full file-list aggregation and may persist seen state while the user watches Changes, adding main-thread work and GC/storage traffic with no visible feature.
Findings.Evidence: `ChangesActivityContribution` is registered AfterRestored and only checks `AgentWorkbenchLayout.Desktop`. Its autorun calls `readLoadedSessionInputPillStats`, and the registered view item observes `pillStats`; both aggregate the active file list. If the Changes editor is visible, the same autorun calls `SeenChangesStore.set`, which clones/serializes the history and writes application storage. The setting is checked only by `SessionActivityBar` when toggling CSS visibility, so these observers remain live while it is off.
Findings.Recommendation: Tie these observers and the seen-store/view-item registration to an observable `sessions.showSessionActivityBar` lifetime (dispose them when disabled and recreate/seed the current baseline when enabled), rather than gating only on desktop layout.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The caller condition, full-history serialization, and storage coalescing semantics are directly traced. Snapshot frequency and URI lengths vary, so severity is low rather than suppressing the proven mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Map/array/object allocations and JSON bytes for up to 200 chat entries, plus queued application-storage database updates
Findings.PerformanceScaling: While the Changes editor is visible, every distinct stats snapshot rebuilds and serializes H history entries, for O(U×H) allocations/bytes with H capped at 200; the storage layer coalesces physical updates on a 100 ms delay but cannot avoid the caller's per-update clone and JSON serialization.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: avoidable main-thread CPU/GC pressure and bursty persisted-state I/O during live edits
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no per-chat seen-state history and no serialization/storage write tied to live change-stat updates.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Watching the Changes tab during an agent turn now clones the history map, maps all entries to new objects, JSON-serializes it, and schedules application-storage persistence for every changed stats value.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 103 serializes and stores the entire bounded map on every `SeenChangesStore.set`; the new autorun calls `set` whenever `activeChanges` updates while `isViewing` is true.
Findings.Title: Coalesce seen-state serialization before writing storage
Findings.Impact: With a populated history, live edit snapshots while Changes is open repeatedly allocate and stringify the same mostly unchanged history, increasing GC and potentially causing small UI stalls; sustained updates also keep scheduling database flushes.
Findings.Evidence: `activeChanges` depends on the live changed-file list. Its autorun unconditionally calls `seenChanges.set` while the matching Changes editor is visible. A changed insertion/deletion count bypasses the equality fast path, after which `set` clones the map and serializes all entries. `Storage.set` updates its cache synchronously and only coalesces the eventual database flush, so the allocation/serialization remains per snapshot.
Findings.Recommendation: Update the in-memory observable immediately, but debounce/coalesce serialization at the store boundary and flush the latest snapshot on the existing save-state/shutdown lifecycle (or on leaving the viewed chat), preserving durability without serializing every intermediate count.

Scenarios.Scenario: Active agent turn updates file changes while the Session Activity Bar setting is disabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Incoming active-chat file-edit snapshots invalidate the selected changeset, then the new `activeChanges` and hover-stat observers synchronously aggregate the complete file list on the renderer thread. This work completes before observable reactions settle; storage work occurs only for baseline seeding or if Changes is visible.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Observe active agent-host chat/changes state snapshots through the existing active-session subscription
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared active-session state subscription; each file-edit snapshot fans into the new local stats observers. No additional per-file IPC call is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing pill and session UI already observed active changes; the PR adds two additional local full-list consumers but no new explicit remote invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Incoming snapshots trigger synchronous local aggregation; the remote subscription itself is pre-existing/shared and is not a new request boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist seen-change baseline in application storage when first observing a chat, and continuously if Changes is visible
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least one write for a cold/unseen active chat; while Changes is visible, one logical store per changed stats snapshot, with physical database updates coalesced by the storage layer's 100 ms delay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No seen-change key or corresponding persistence existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Map cloning and JSON serialization are synchronous; the database flush is asynchronous/off the immediate critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of distinct live edit snapshots U and effective changed-file cardinality F after the provider merges streaming and authoritative changes. The two new aggregations each scan F entries, yielding O(U×F), potentially O(F²) as files accumulate.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable reactions are synchronous and serialized on the renderer thread. Provider state uses one shared active-session subscription; the diff adds consumers rather than parallel remote calls. No limiter or deferral protects the aggregation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing stats cache can supply a restored pill only before authoritative data exists; it does not cache aggregate results for a live file-list identity. Cold startup loads the seen map once, while warm runs reuse that map, but both new reductions rerun on every distinct snapshot. The disabled setting does not suppress them.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the missing configuration gate, synchronous observable call paths, two collection reductions, and setting default are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical turn file counts and edit-snapshot frequency vary, but stable builds default this feature off, making all observed cost wasted for that population.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable eager work and repeated work: the new contribution runs despite the feature being disabled and performs duplicate complete aggregations on live updates.

Scenarios.Scenario: User keeps the Changes tab visible while an agent edits files
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each changed stats snapshot is aggregated, recognized as viewed, copied into the seen map, transformed into a full history array, and JSON-serialized synchronously. The actual storage database flush is delayed/coalesced, but serialization occurs before the autorun returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Store the complete `sessions.changesActivity.seenChanges` JSON value in application storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical store per distinct stats update while viewed; database persistence is coalesced to the latest pending value on the storage service delay.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The scenario performed no seen-history serialization or database update before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: JSON construction is on the critical renderer path; database I/O is asynchronous but sustained updates repeatedly schedule flushes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: U distinct stats snapshots during the turn and H persisted chats after LRU capping (H<=200). Synchronous persistence preparation is O(U×H) objects/bytes, in addition to O(U×F) stats aggregation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The autorun and serialization are synchronous and serialized on the renderer. Storage keeps only the latest pending value per key and flushes after a 100 ms throttled delay, bounding simultaneous database operations but not caller allocations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold history loads/parses once. Warm history can contain 200 entries; every changed stats value clones and serializes all of them. Equal stats for the newest chat short-circuit, but actual live insertion/deletion count changes miss that fast path. There is no pre-storage debounce.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the viewing condition and full-map serialization are direct, and storage implementation confirms only the database flush—not JSON work—is coalesced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The 200-entry cap bounds each serialization, and physical writes are coalesced; actual pause size depends on chat-resource string lengths and snapshot rate.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable serialization/allocation regression; persistence should be coalesced before rebuilding the full stored value.

Scenarios.Scenario: Session switching/restoration with the Changes tab hidden
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Selecting a loaded chat computes aggregate stats, loads or looks up its persisted baseline, and seeds an unseen chat once. Badge transitions notify activity view items and update badge/tooltip DOM; no filesystem/network request blocks selection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the application-storage seen-history cache and persist a newly seeded chat baseline
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded read on contribution construction and at most one logical write when a chat lacks a baseline; repeated equal stats for the newest chat are skipped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Read/JSON parse and baseline serialization are synchronous during contribution/selection; database write flush is asynchronous.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active chat at a time, changed-file cardinality F, seen-history H<=200, and number of rendered activity-bar entries across visible chat groups.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Selection reactions are synchronous. Badge events fan synchronously to registered action items, each filtering by command id; no parallel I/O burst occurs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold startup parses the bounded seen JSON and may seed one baseline; warm startup uses the loaded map. The first observation intentionally negative-caches a baseline. Session stats fallback uses the existing 30-session cache only while authoritative changes are unavailable.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for costs and lifecycle. Badge DOM fanout is bounded by currently constructed chat groups and did not establish a separate high-impact finding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Normal histories and changed-file lists are often small; worst-case bounds are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding beyond the setting gate/repeated aggregation/persistence findings; badge rendering and listener cleanup are disposed with their view items and service handles.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hovering or theme-changing the Changes activity entry
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The custom view item reads already-derived stats and creates a small hover DOM subtree on demand; theme/activity changes update badge classes, colors, text, aria label, and managed-hover content synchronously.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of constructed activity bars and their menu entries; hover content itself is constant-size and independent of file count because it consumes aggregate stats.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All DOM updates are synchronous renderer work; global activity events fan to listeners but filter by command id. There is no queue or boundary call.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Aggregate stats are held by a derived observable and equality-compared. Hover DOM is created only when requested by the managed hover callback; no unbounded DOM cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the path is local DOM work; insufficient magnitude for another reportable synchronous-UI finding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users can construct several chat groups/session views, but visible screen layout bounds realistic counts and badge transitions are infrequent.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate performance finding; work is constant per view item and lifecycle-owned.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 17 changed files and traced live edit, disabled-feature, visible-Changes persistence, restoration, badge rendering, cache, listener, and boundary behavior. Submitted three diff-caused findings: unconditional work while the activity bar is off, duplicate full-list aggregation per live edit, and uncoalesced full-history serialization while Changes is visible. No qualifying regression fix was present.
